integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A static, low-angle black-and-white composition of a still puddle resting on wet cobblestone during a soft, steady rainfall. The camera frames the water surface so concentric raindrop ripples dominate the lower two-thirds of the frame, while a single autumn leaf — dark, veined, slightly curled — floats near the right edge of the puddle, half-submerged. Raindrops strike the puddle at irregular intervals, each impact generating a fresh circular wavelet that expands outward, intersects with prior ripples, and produces the visible interference pattern of overlapping rings — crests brightening where rings meet, troughs darkening where opposing waves cancel. A few drops strike the leaf directly. The combined wave energy from the colliding ripples gently lifts, slides, and rotates the leaf a few centimeters across the surface, the leaf rocking as successive wavefronts pass beneath it, then settling for a moment before the next drop arrives. The background is a soft, out-of-focus suggestion of rain falling on darker wet pavement, with light catching wet stones to create quiet, contemplative highlights; a faint silhouette of a curb or step anchors the upper edge of the frame. The film grain is subtle, the tonality high-contrast, the mood intimate and observational.

overall_soundscape: Steady, soft patter of rain on stone and water; the distinct higher-pitched plip of individual drops striking the puddle surface; the gentle lap and slosh as wave ripples reach the leaf and stone edges; the faint, wet scrape of the leaf rocking on the water; a distant muted hush of rain falling on the wider wet environment.
